newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-RISING STAR PESLIER SET TO LAND FIRST ARC.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-RISING STAR PESLIER SET TO LAND FIRST ARC.

text.p: Rising star Olivier Peslier is convinced he has what it takes to give him a first win this weekend's Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Europe's richest race.
Peslier finished a close second last year to Lammtarra on Freedom Cry, but Helissio, his Longchamp mount on Sunday, has an outstanding chance and is currently a well fancied 5-2 favourite.
Peslier said: "Helissio has a lot going for him. He can travel close to the pace or be held up. He is very adaptable in that sense, but the important thing with him is not to contradict him.
"And the ground, which has turned very soft following the recent rain, shouldn't worry him. I think he can act on most surfaces."
Helissio's big races successes this season include the Prix Niel and two group ones, the Prix Lupin and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud.
The colt flopped when favourite for the French Derby, pulling hard and then getting boxed in with Dominique Boeuf on board. But since Peslier took over, Helissio has not looked back.
He holds a clear chance, especially as doubts persist about some of his his leading rivals.
Big-race specialist Michael Kinane has sounded a cautionary note about 5-1 second favourite Zagreb, who will be having only the fourth race of his career.
Zagreb, a surprise but impressive 20-1 winner of the Irish Derby at the end of June, has not raced since.
Kinane said: "It's a slight worry that he goes without a preparatory race and with a lack of experience, but the state of the ground has been the reason we haven't been able to get a run into him."
With the ground likely to ride soft, Zagreb cannot be ignored but the going may be against leading English raider Pentire (8-1).

The colt is a consistent and top-notch performer and won the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes at Ascot in July, beating three of Sunday's rivals -- Classic Cliche (8-1), Shaamit (10-1) and Oscar Schindler (14-1).
Classic Cliche, the Ascot Gold Cup winner, missed some work at the weekend and jockey-of-the-moment Frankie Dettori may switch to 33-1 outsider Tamure if Classic Cliche is ruled out.
Shaamit, an impressive Epsom Derby winner, has failed twice since but Oscar Schindler looked like he was still improving when he won last month's Irish St Leger.

Top French trainer Andre Fabre sends out four of the 20 runners still left in but 11-2 chance Swain, third in last year's Arc and conqueror of Pentire in last month's Prix Foy, looks the brightest of his prospects.

The colt has a length to make up on Helissio on their running at Saint-Cloud in June and Swain looks sure to be in the shake-up, with Thierry Jarnet bidding for a third Arc success following victories in 1992 on Subotica and Carnegie two years ago.
The Aga Khan also holds a sound chance with 6-1 shot Darazari, a facile winner of the Prix Maurice de Nieuil at Maisons-Laffitte in July and not disgraced when second to Helissio in the Prix Niel.

Gallic hearts might melt if English-trained Pilsudski (14-1) were to give jockey Walter Swinburn his first Arc win since 1983. Swinburn was almost killed in an accident in Hong Kong early this year but is back riding as well as ever.
Latest betting: 5-2 Helissio, 5-1 Zagreb, 11-2 Swain, 6-1 Darazari, 8-1 Pentire and Classic Cliche, 10-1 Shaamit, 14-1 Oscar Schindler and Pilsudski, 20-1 and upwards others.
